en: Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha’s consort, the leader of this world,
honored for her maternal nature, whose character is equal to Hari’s,
who brings auspiciousness to the world and possesses a beautiful form.
I take refuge in the Blessed Lady whose abode is the lotus. 1.

On the peak of Mount Śrīyāda, two physicians for the disease of worldly existence— filled with the weight of devotion to their followers and constantly radiant— arose through the extraordinary penance of the lord of sages named Śrīyāda.
I take refuge at the feet of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha. 2.
Though the forms of the gods were transformed, these two remained their own ageless selves; they are the most excellent of all, worthy of being served by the virtuous,
the life-givers of everyone, and identical in nature.
I take refuge at the feet of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha. 3.
O Śrī, you who are the abode of compassion and expert in protecting those who have sought refuge, the two Sahakāra trees at the entrance to the Lakṣmīśata temple are even more beloved than you.
I take refuge at the feet of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha. 4.

O grandson of Prahlāda, O Dānava Bali! You have manifested at this time the giving of land, which reveals the inferior nature of others and establishes the standard for the world, bringing auspiciousness to the gods.
I take refuge at the feet of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha. 5.
Having cast off the body, the two royal swans of pure mind sport upon the sprouts of the Kalpa-tree of Vedānta;
they are proclaimed as the root-wealth of true devotees, possessing such great power.
I take refuge at the feet of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha. 6.
Thus ends "The Prayer of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha of Yādagiri," composed by the venerable Narasiṃhācārya of Vaṅgīpura.
